title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Wrong words in the unused code summaries
summary: The command that reports everything unused printed its own detector keys, and every label inside those summaries only knew the plural.

highlights.title: The summary named its own internals
highlights.description: Detector keys such as writeOnly and locals reached the notification instead of the words for them. On a project of 5093 Kotlin and Java files it read 43 locals, 21 imports, 19 declarations, 4 writeOnly, 2 parameters.

highlights.title: Nine labels that only knew the plural
highlights.description: A single result read 1 dead islands, 1 enum entries, 1 catalog aliases. Each label carries its own singular now, since entrys and aliass would follow from any rule that guesses one.

highlights.title: Two sentences that ended badly
highlights.description: The per file clean up line agreed its count in the previous release and left the verb behind. With every check empty and one check skipped, the summary ended on a colon with nothing after it.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The aggregate unused code summary shows the label of each dead code detector, not its key, and shares that table with the command that reports the same scan.
Nine section labels and five detector labels now carry a singular, so one finding reads 1 dead island, 1 enum entry, 1 catalog alias, 1 write-only variable.
The per file clean up message no longer disagrees with its own count when a single finding needs a manual fix.
The count of freed version catalog entries agrees at one.
With nothing found and a check skipped, the summary no longer ends on a colon followed by a full stop.
